key_insight: A phononic subsurface embedded in a flat plate can passively reshape sustained vortex shedding, with its position and resonant growth rate tuning the flow between amplification and strong attenuation regimes.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a passive control strategy for reducing unsteady lift and drag in separated-flow systems without materially changing mean aerodynamic loads.
method: High-fidelity immersed boundary simulations of fully separated flow over a flat plate with a compliant section driven by a grounded diatomic-chain phononic subsurface.
Parameter sweep over chordwise subsurface position and resonant displacement growth rate.
Analysis of limit-cycle behavior, lift/drag oscillations, phase relations, frequencies, and mean/unsteady flow fields.
evidence_signal: The simulations identified four position-dependent limit-cycle regimes, including one case with over 30% lower lift oscillation and over 50% lower drag oscillation while mean lift and drag changed by less than 0.5%.
watch_item: The reported benefits are highly sensitive to subsurface placement and resonance characteristics, so performance may not generalize without careful design and flow-condition matching.
paper_title: Interaction of Sustained Vortex Shedding with a Phononic Subsurface: Effect of Positioning and Resonant Characteristics
